# breedtools

Design and analysis of plant breeding trials, from single trials to
groups of environments, with storage in ‘Breedbase’.

- **Design** augmented row-column, augmented p-rep and resolvable
  row-column trials, or bring designs made with ‘agricolae’.
- **Analyse** each trial (adjusted means, BLUPs, spatial models with
  ‘SpATS’) and several trials together (two-stage or single-stage).
- **Group environments** that rank genotypes alike (Lin, 1982) and draw
  them on a map.
- **Save** trials, phenotypes and analysis results to ‘Breedbase’
  through BrAPI.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("solgenomics/breedtools")
library(breedtools)
```

## Connect to Breedbase (optional)

Designs, analyses and environment groups all work offline. A connection
is only needed to check names against your database, save trials,
phenotypes and results, or read phenotypes from it. You need an account
on the site; use a test site such as
`https://cassava-test.sgn.cornell.edu` to try things out before saving
to production.

``` r

con <- breedbase_login("https://cassavabase.org", username = "your_username")
con                          # site, user and time of login
breedbase_programs(con)      # breeding programs your account can see
breedbase_folders(con, program = "IITA")
breedbase_locations(con)
```

Never write your password in a script: leave it out and type it in the
pop-up, or set `BREEDBASE_PASSWORD` in your `.Renviron` file. Test sites
also have a web password (`site_username`, `BREEDBASE_SITE_PASSWORD`).
[`?breedbase_connection`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_connection.md)
explains every option.

## Designs from breedtools

| Design | When to use it | Function |
|----|----|----|
| Augmented row-column (Piepho and Williams, 2016) | One plot per entry, replicated checks, one location | [`augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_design.md) |
| Augmented p-rep (Williams, Piepho and Whitaker, 2011) | Several locations, part of the entries repeated, no checks | [`augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_design.md) |
| Resolvable row-column (Williams, John and Whitaker, 2006) | Every entry in every replicate | [`resolvable_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/resolvable_row_column_design.md) |

Not sure which layout fits? Start from the number of entries:

``` r

design_options(n_entries = 100)  # field dimensions and checks not yet known
design_options(108, design = "augmented_row_column", n_checks = 4, rows_in_field = 12, cols_in_field = 12)
design_options(42, design = "resolvable", n_reps = 3, cols_in_field = 7)
```

Then generate the design, look at the field map, check it and save it:

``` r

rc <- augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments = sprintf("LINE_%03d", 1:108),
  controls = c("CHECK_A", "CHECK_B", "CHECK_C", "CHECK_D"),
  rows_in_field = 12, cols_in_field = 12,
  rows_per_block = 4, cols_per_block = 4,
  seed = 2026
)
plot_augmented_row_column_design(rc)

# Save it to Breedbase: check the names, preview, then save
breedbase_check(con, accessions = rc, location = "Ibadan", program = "IITA",
                folder = "AYT 2026", trial_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan")
save_breedbase(rc, con, program = "IITA", folder = "AYT 2026",
               trial_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan", year = 2026, location = "Ibadan",
               description = "Advanced yield trial", dry_run = TRUE)
save_breedbase(rc, con, program = "IITA", folder = "AYT 2026",
               trial_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan", year = 2026, location = "Ibadan",
               description = "Advanced yield trial")
sheet <- phenotype_template(rc, trial_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan", location = "Ibadan",
                            traits = "fresh root yield")   # field sheet with the plot names
```

Augmented row-column designs can have unequal row and column groups, any
number of check plots per block and D-optimal check placement. P-rep
designs are built by a randomized search or from the paper’s alpha and
alpha(2) arrays (`method`), and report their efficiency factor.
Resolvable designs are optimized for row-column and spatial efficiency,
with latinized options.
[`add_plot_coordinates()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_plot_coordinates.md)
adds GPS coordinates to the plots before saving.

## Designs from agricolae

Designs generated with the CRAN package ‘agricolae’ keep their
randomization and use the same saving workflow:

``` r

accessions <- c("G1", "G2", "G3", "CHECK_A")  # existing Breedbase accession names
randomized <- agricolae::design.rcbd(accessions, r = 3, seed = 2026)
trial <- prepare_breedbase_trial(
  randomized, trial_name = "RCBD_2026", year = 2026,
  location = "Ibadan", program = "Your breeding program",
  description = "RCBD with three complete blocks generated with agricolae",
  checks = "CHECK_A", prompt = FALSE
)

payload <- save_breedbase(trial, dry_run = TRUE)   # preview, no connection needed
save_breedbase(trial, con, dry_run = TRUE)         # check against your database
save_breedbase(trial, con)                         # save as a new trial
```

[`prepare_breedbase_trial()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_breedbase_trial.md)
records the trial information once and converts the field book. In an
interactive RStudio session it can ask for the missing name, year,
location, program and description. It recognizes CRD, RCBD, alpha,
lattice, augmented block, split-plot and strip-plot designs. For a field
book alone, including
[`agricolae::zigzag()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/agricolae/man/zigzag.html)
output, supply `design_type`. For several treatment factors, name the
accession column, e.g. `accession = "genotype"`; the other factors stay
in `trial$book`. See
[`?as_breedbase_design`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/as_breedbase_design.md)
for the column mapping.

## Analysis

Each design has its own analysis: ANOVA with estimable degrees of
freedom, adjusted entry means (BLUEs) with standard errors, the mean SED
and the 5% LSD, or random entries (BLUPs) and ‘SpATS’ spatial models.

``` r

field <- rc$design
field$yield <- rnorm(nrow(field), 60, 3)   # your phenotypes here
plot_trait(field, "yield")                 # distribution and field map
find_outliers(field, "yield")
fit <- analyze_augmented_row_column_design(field, response = "yield")
fit                                        # ANOVA and top adjusted means
fit$adjusted_means                         # all entries ranked
```

For trials of any design across locations,
[`analyze_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_two_stage.md)
analyses each location first (spatial, blocks or design model) and then
combines them, weighting by precision and with a random
genotype-by-location interaction;
[`analyze_single_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_single_stage.md)
fits everything in one model. P-rep designs have their own
[`analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage.md).

The results go back to Breedbase, with the phenotypes:

``` r

save_breedbase_phenotypes(sheet, con)                  # the field sheet, filled in
stage1 <- first_stage_values(fit, rc, trial_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan",
                             location = "Ibadan", trait = "fresh root yield")
save_breedbase_first_stage(stage1, con)                # adjusted plot values
stage2 <- second_stage_values(fit, trait = "fresh root yield")
save_breedbase_analysis(stage2, con, analysis_name = "AYT_2026_Ibadan_means",
                        program = "IITA", description = "Adjusted means, row-column model")
```

Every `save_*()` function accepts `dry_run = TRUE` to check everything
without writing.

## Environment stratification (grouping environments)

Before combining trials from several locations, check two things: are
the error variances similar enough to analyse the trials together, and
which environments rank the genotypes alike? Both run directly on a
phenotype file downloaded from ‘Breedbase’. The package includes an
example with four trials:

``` r

pheno_file <- system.file("extdata", "breedbase_pheno.csv", package = "breedtools")
loc_file   <- system.file("extdata", "breedbase_locations.csv", package = "breedtools")

# 1. Homogeneity of error variances (Hartley's Fmax, simulated critical value)
vc <- run_breedbase_variance_check(pheno_file, trait_col = "fresh root yield|CO_334:0000013")
vc$overall_hartley              # all four together: Fmax 5.66 > 5.20, not homogeneous
vc$maximal_compatible_groups    # largest sets of trials that can be combined

# 2. Group environments by genotype-by-environment interaction (Lin, 1982)
st <- run_environment_stratification(pheno_file, trait = "fresh root yield")
st$group_summary
#>   group_id      locations n_env    ms_ge   f_value    p_value
#> 1  Group_1 Geneva, Ithaca     2 2.259034 1.8924496 0.09774358
#> 2  Group_2 Ibadan, Ubiaja     2 4.422801 0.7875387 0.64998303

# 3. Draw the groups on an interactive map (open maps, no API key)
map_environment_groups(st, read_locations(loc_file, phenotype_data = st))
```

![Environment groups of the example trials on a map: Geneva and Ithaca
(New York) form Group 1, Ibadan and Ubiaja (Nigeria) form Group
2.](reference/figures/README-environment-groups.png)

Environment groups of the example trials on a map: Geneva and Ithaca
(New York) form Group 1, Ibadan and Ubiaja (Nigeria) form Group 2.

Environments in the same group have a non-significant GxE between them,
so they can be treated as one target environment. Your own file works
the same way: download the phenotypes of the trials from ‘Breedbase’
(`.csv` or `.xlsx`) and pass its path; columns are detected
automatically.
`run_environment_stratification(..., export_json = TRUE, output_dir = ...)`
also saves the results as JSON.

## Documentation

- **Website**: <https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/>. The
  [function
  reference](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/) groups
  every function by task and shows its arguments with examples you can
  run.
- **Tutorial**:
  [`vignette("breedtools")`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/articles/breedtools.md)
  walks through every design and analysis with simulated data, and
  connecting to Breedbase.
- **RStudio script**: the whole workflow in one file,
  `file.edit(system.file("examples", "breedtools_workflow.R", package = "breedtools"))`.
  The complete tour in `scripts/validate_designs.R` (in the GitHub
  repository) also reads existing Breedbase trials and adds traits to
  saved analyses.
- **In R**:
  [`help(package = "breedtools")`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference)
  lists every help page.
  [`?augmented_row_column_design`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_design.md)
  opens one page, and `example(augmented_row_column_design)` runs its
  examples.

## All functions

Each function has a help page with runnable examples: `?function_name`,
then `example(function_name)`. Functions that connect to Breedbase have
examples in `\dontrun{}`. To run them, you need a server and an account.

### 1. Choose a design

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`design_options()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/design_options.md) | Suggests layouts for any design from the number of entries and the field size, if you know it |
| [`augmented_row_column_capacity()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_capacity.md) | Counts the entries and checks that fit in an augmented row-column field |
| [`augmented_row_column_layouts()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_layouts.md) | Lists the analyzable block layouts of an augmented row-column field |
| [`augmented_prep_parameters()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_parameters.md) | Lists feasible settings for the alpha and alpha(2) p-rep constructions |

``` r

design_options(n_entries = 100)
augmented_row_column_layouts(rows_in_field = 12, cols_in_field = 12)
augmented_prep_parameters(n_treatments = 20, n_locations = 2)
```

### 2. Augmented row-column designs (one plot per entry, replicated checks)

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_design.md) | Generates the design with D-optimal or Latin check placement |
| [`plot_augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_augmented_row_column_design.md) | Draws the field map |
| [`analyze_augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_row_column_design.md) | ANOVA and adjusted means using fixed or random blocks, random entries (BLUPs), or a SpATS model |

``` r

rc <- augmented_row_column_design(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4),
                                  rows_in_field = 12, cols_in_field = 12,
                                  rows_per_block = 4, cols_per_block = 4, seed = 1)
plot_augmented_row_column_design(rc)
d <- rc$design; d$yield <- rnorm(nrow(d), 50, 3)
fit <- analyze_augmented_row_column_design(d, "yield")
fit$adjusted_means
```

### 3. Augmented p-rep designs (several locations, part of the entries repeated)

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_design.md) | Generates the design (`method = "search"`, `"alpha"` or `"alpha2"`) |
| [`augmented_prep_concurrence()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_concurrence.md) | Counts how often each pair of entries shares a block |
| [`plot_augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_augmented_prep_design.md) | Draws the field map of each location |
| [`analyze_augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_prep_design.md) | Single-stage analysis with optional genotype-by-location interaction |
| [`analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage.md) | Two-stage analysis with heterogeneous error variances and optional SpATS |

``` r

prep <- augmented_prep_design(paste0("G", 1:60), locations = c("North", "South"),
                              block_size = 6, field_cols = 10, seed = 1)
plot_augmented_prep_design(prep)
d <- prep$design; d$yield <- rnorm(nrow(d), 25, 3)
analyze_augmented_prep_design(d, "yield")
analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(d, "yield")
```

### 4. Resolvable row-column designs (fully replicated)

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`resolvable_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/resolvable_row_column_design.md) | Generates a spatially optimized design, including latinized options |
| [`resolvable_row_column_efficiency()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/resolvable_row_column_efficiency.md) | Calculates row-column, linear variance and AR efficiencies of a design |
| [`plot_resolvable_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_resolvable_row_column_design.md) | Draws the field map |
| [`analyze_resolvable_row_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_resolvable_row_column.md) | Fits RC, LV + RC or AR + RC models by REML |

``` r

rr <- resolvable_row_column_design(paste0("T", 1:42), n_reps = 3,
                                   rows_per_rep = 6, cols_per_rep = 7, seed = 1)
resolvable_row_column_efficiency(rr)
plot_resolvable_row_column_design(rr)
d <- rr$design; d$yield <- rnorm(nrow(d), 40, 4)
analyze_resolvable_row_column(d, "yield", model = "rc")   # or "lv", "ar"
```

### 5. Analysis for any design

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`plot_trait()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_trait.md) | Plots a trait’s distribution and field map |
| [`find_outliers()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/find_outliers.md) / [`remove_outliers()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/remove_outliers.md) | Flags or removes outlying plots with the IQR rule |
| [`analyze_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_two_stage.md) | Two-stage analysis of several trials of any design |
| [`analyze_single_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_single_stage.md) | Single-stage analysis of several trials, as an alternative |
| [`compare_first_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/compare_first_stage.md) | Compares raw and first-stage adjusted plot values |
| [`first_stage_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/first_stage_values.md) | Returns the adjusted plot values to store as a trait |
| [`second_stage_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/second_stage_values.md) | Returns the genotype values to store as a Breedbase analysis |
| [`prediction_accuracy()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prediction_accuracy.md) | Correlates adjusted means with known (simulated) genotype values |

``` r

plot_trait(d, "yield")
find_outliers(d, "yield")
fit2 <- analyze_two_stage(met, "yield", stage1 = "design")  # met: trials stacked with a location column
second_stage_values(fit2, trait = "fresh root yield")
```

### 6. Design checks

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`check_setup()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_setup.md) | Checks that packages and the output folder are ready |
| [`check_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_design.md) | Runs the standard checks on any design, such as plot use, entry counts, check placement and estimable effects |
| [`check_section()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_section.md) / [`check_result()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_result.md) | Labels a section and records your own checks |
| [`check_summary()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_summary.md) / [`check_reset()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_reset.md) | Prints or clears the recorded checklist |

``` r

check_reset(); check_design(rc); check_summary()
```

### 7. Breedbase: connect, look up and save designs

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`breedbase_login()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_login.md) | Logs in to a Breedbase server through BrAPI |
| [`breedbase_programs()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md) / [`breedbase_folders()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md) / [`breedbase_locations()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md) | Lists breeding programs, trial folders and locations |
| [`breedbase_check()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_check.md) | Checks the program, folder, location, accessions, trial and plot names before you save, and says whether everything is READY |
| [`add_plot_names()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_plot_names.md) | Adds the Breedbase plot names to a design, to see, check or edit them before saving |
| [`add_plot_coordinates()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_plot_coordinates.md) | Adds plot GPS coordinates, from the field corner and plot size, or one point per plot |
| [`save_breedbase_coordinates()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_coordinates.md) | Saves plot GPS coordinates to a trial already in Breedbase |
| [`prepare_breedbase_trial()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_breedbase_trial.md) | Converts an agricolae design and records the trial information |
| [`as_breedbase_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/as_breedbase_design.md) | Converts an agricolae field book only (column mapping) |
| [`save_breedbase()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase.md) | Saves a design as a new trial with its plots and their GPS coordinates (`dry_run = TRUE` previews it) |
| [`breedbase_trial_plots()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_trial_plots.md) | Reads the plots of a saved trial |
| [`phenotype_template()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/phenotype_template.md) | Makes a phenotyping sheet with the Breedbase plot names |

``` r

con <- breedbase_login("https://your-breedbase.org", "your_username")
breedbase_programs(con)
rc <- add_plot_names(rc, "AYT_2026", location = "Ibadan")       # see rc$design$plot_name
rc <- add_plot_coordinates(rc, origin = c(7.4931, 3.9035), plot_width = 3, plot_length = 5)
breedbase_check(con, accessions = rc, location = "Ibadan", program = "Cassava",
                trial_name = "AYT_2026")
save_breedbase(rc, con, program = "Cassava", folder = "AYT 2026",
               trial_name = "AYT_2026", year = 2026, location = "Ibadan",
               description = "Advanced yield trial", dry_run = TRUE)
phenotype_template(rc, traits = "fresh root yield")      # uses the stored plot names
```

### 8. Breedbase: phenotypes and analysis results

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`breedbase_phenotypes()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_phenotypes.md) | Reads phenotypes of trials by trial and trait name |
| [`save_breedbase_phenotypes()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_phenotypes.md) | Saves phenotypes by plot and trait name |
| [`save_breedbase_first_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_first_stage.md) | Saves first-stage plot values as a trait of the field plots |
| [`save_breedbase_analysis()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_analysis.md) | Saves results as a Breedbase analysis, of plots (first stage) or accessions (second stage) |
| [`analysis_plot_names()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analysis_plot_names.md) | Shows the plot and accession names an analysis will have, before saving |
| [`breedbase_analysis_plots()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_analysis_plots.md) | Reads the plots, accessions and values of an analysis already in Breedbase |
| [`add_breedbase_analysis_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_breedbase_analysis_values.md) | Adds another trait to an existing analysis |
| [`breedbase_statistics()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_statistics.md) | Lists the statistic terms of the SGNSTAT ontology |
| [`breedbase_adjusted_trait()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_adjusted_trait.md) | Finds or creates the trait used for adjusted values |
| [`breedbase_refresh()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_refresh.md) | Refreshes the server’s phenotype cache |

### 9. Multi-environment trials from Breedbase files

| Function | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`read_breedbase_file()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_breedbase_file.md) / [`read_breedbase_excel()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_breedbase_excel.md) | Reads Breedbase phenotype or design files (Excel, CSV, TSV) |
| [`prepare_breedbase_pheno()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_breedbase_pheno.md) | Prepares phenotypes for multi-environment analysis |
| [`run_breedbase_variance_check()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_breedbase_variance_check.md) | Analyzes each environment, runs Hartley’s Fmax test and finds compatible groups |
| [`run_environment_stratification()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_environment_stratification.md) | Groups environments by GxE using Lin (1982) |
| [`run_breedbase_environment_stratification()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_breedbase_environment_stratification.md) | Runs the same grouping directly from a Breedbase file |
| [`read_locations()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_locations.md) / [`map_environment_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/map_environment_groups.md) | Loads location coordinates and draws the groups on a map |

``` r

pheno_file <- system.file("extdata", "breedbase_pheno.csv", package = "breedtools")
loc_file   <- system.file("extdata", "breedbase_locations.csv", package = "breedtools")
vc <- run_breedbase_variance_check(pheno_file, trait_col = "fresh root yield|CO_334:0000013")
vc$maximal_compatible_groups
st <- run_environment_stratification(pheno_file, trait = "fresh root yield")
map_environment_groups(st, read_locations(loc_file, phenotype_data = st))
```

### 10. Building blocks and helpers

The pipeline functions above call these lower-level functions. You can
call them yourself to run one step at a time.

| Group | Functions |
|----|----|
| Variance check | [`analyze_environment_anova()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_environment_anova.md), [`analyze_one_environment()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_one_environment.md), [`hartley_fmax_test()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/hartley_fmax_test.md), [`hartley_critical_sim()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/hartley_critical_sim.md), [`make_environment_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/make_environment_groups.md), [`get_compatible_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/get_compatible_groups.md), [`get_maximal_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/get_maximal_groups.md), [`harmonic_mean()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/harmonic_mean.md) |
| Environment stratification | [`prepare_environment_stratification_data()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_environment_stratification_data.md), [`detect_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/detect_design.md), [`prepare_design_factors()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_design_factors.md), [`calculate_environment_stratification_anova()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/calculate_environment_stratification_anova.md), [`lin_group_environments()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_group_environments.md), [`lin_test_group()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_test_group.md), [`lin_ss_ge()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_ss_ge.md), [`lin_error_mse()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_error_mse.md), [`complete_environment_info()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/complete_environment_info.md), [`add_environment_metadata()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_environment_metadata.md), [`add_pairwise_environment_metadata()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_pairwise_environment_metadata.md), [`environment_summary_by_group()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/environment_summary_by_group.md) |
| Columns and empty tables | [`find_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/find_column.md), [`guess_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/guess_column.md), [`normalize_column_name()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/normalize_column_name.md), [`empty_anova()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/empty_anova.md), [`empty_group_membership()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/empty_group_membership.md), [`empty_group_summary()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/empty_group_summary.md), [`empty_pairwise()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/empty_pairwise.md), [`empty_ungrouped()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/empty_ungrouped.md) |

# Package index

## Choose a design

Start from the number of entries and the field space you have.

- [`design_options()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/design_options.md)
  : Suggest trial layouts from the number of entries and available field
  space
- [`augmented_row_column_capacity()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_capacity.md)
  : Calculate augmented row-column design capacity
- [`augmented_row_column_layouts()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_layouts.md)
  : List the analyzable layouts of an augmented row-column field
- [`augmented_prep_parameters()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_parameters.md)
  : Feasible parameters for augmented p-rep constructions

## Augmented row-column designs

Unreplicated entries plus replicated checks in rows, columns and blocks
(Federer, Nair and Raghavarao 1975; Piepho and Williams 2016).

- [`augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_row_column_design.md)
  : Generate an augmented row-column field design
- [`plot_augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_augmented_row_column_design.md)
  : Plot an augmented row-column design grid
- [`analyze_augmented_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_row_column_design.md)
  : Analyze an augmented row-column design
- [`print(`*`<augmented_row_column_analysis>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.augmented_row_column_analysis.md)
  : Print augmented row-column analysis

## Augmented p-rep designs

Multi-location partially replicated designs (Williams, Piepho and
Whitaker 2011).

- [`augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_design.md)
  : Generate an augmented p-rep design
- [`augmented_prep_concurrence()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/augmented_prep_concurrence.md)
  : Calculate pairwise concurrence for a p-rep design
- [`plot_augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_augmented_prep_design.md)
  : Plot an augmented p-rep design grid
- [`analyze_augmented_prep_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_prep_design.md)
  : Analyze an augmented p-rep design
- [`analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage.md)
  : Two-stage analysis of a multi-location augmented p-rep trial
- [`print(`*`<augmented_prep_analysis>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.augmented_prep_analysis.md)
  : Print augmented p-rep analysis
- [`print(`*`<augmented_prep_two_stage>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.augmented_prep_two_stage.md)
  : Print a two-stage p-rep analysis

## Resolvable row-column designs

Fully replicated spatial designs (Williams, John and Whitaker 2006).

- [`resolvable_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/resolvable_row_column_design.md)
  : Generate a resolvable (spatial) row-column design
- [`resolvable_row_column_efficiency()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/resolvable_row_column_efficiency.md)
  : Efficiency of a resolvable row-column design
- [`plot_resolvable_row_column_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_resolvable_row_column_design.md)
  : Plot a resolvable row-column design
- [`analyze_resolvable_row_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_resolvable_row_column.md)
  : Analyze a resolvable row-column trial with RC, LV + RC or AR + RC
  models
- [`print(`*`<resolvable_row_column_analysis>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.resolvable_row_column_analysis.md)
  : Print a resolvable row-column analysis

## Analysis for any design

Trait plots, outliers, two-stage and single-stage analysis of several
trials, and the values to store from them.

- [`plot_trait()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/plot_trait.md)
  : Plot a trait: boxplot, distribution and field map
- [`find_outliers()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/find_outliers.md)
  : Find outliers in trait data (IQR rule)
- [`remove_outliers()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/remove_outliers.md)
  : Remove outliers from trait data (IQR rule)
- [`analyze_two_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_two_stage.md)
  : Two-stage analysis of a multi-location trial, for any design
- [`analyze_single_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_single_stage.md)
  : Single-stage analysis of several trials
- [`compare_first_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/compare_first_stage.md)
  : Compare raw and first-stage adjusted values
- [`first_stage_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/first_stage_values.md)
  : First-stage plot values from an analysis
- [`second_stage_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/second_stage_values.md)
  : Second-stage genotype values from analyses
- [`prediction_accuracy()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prediction_accuracy.md)
  : Accuracy of adjusted means against known values
- [`print(`*`<two_stage_analysis>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.two_stage_analysis.md)
  : Print a two-stage analysis
- [`print(`*`<single_stage_analysis>`*`)`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/print.single_stage_analysis.md)
  : Print a single-stage analysis

## Design checks

Verify a design and record a checklist of what was tested.

- [`check_setup()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_setup.md)
  : Check that everything is ready before starting
- [`check_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_design.md)
  : Standard checks of a design
- [`check_section()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_section.md)
  : Set the section label for the next checks
- [`check_result()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_result.md)
  : Record and print a check
- [`check_summary()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_summary.md)
  : Summary of the recorded checks
- [`check_reset()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/check_reset.md)
  : Clear the recorded checks

## Breedbase connection and lookups

Log in through BrAPI, list programs, folders and locations, and check
names before designing.

- [`breedbase_connection`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_connection.md)
  : Connecting to a Breedbase instance
- [`breedbase_login()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_login.md)
  : Log in to a Breedbase server
- [`breedbase_programs()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md)
  [`breedbase_folders()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md)
  [`breedbase_locations()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_lists.md)
  : List breeding programs, folders and locations in Breedbase
- [`breedbase_check()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_check.md)
  : Check names in Breedbase before building a design
- [`breedbase_statistics()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_statistics.md)
  : List the statistic terms of Breedbase (SGNSTAT ontology)
- [`breedbase_adjusted_trait()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_adjusted_trait.md)
  : Find or create the Breedbase trait for adjusted values
- [`breedbase_refresh()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_refresh.md)
  : Refresh the Breedbase phenotype cache

## Save designs to Breedbase

Convert agricolae designs, add plot names and GPS coordinates, preview
the payload, and save trials with their plots.

- [`prepare_breedbase_trial()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_breedbase_trial.md)
  : Prepare an agricolae design and trial information for Breedbase
- [`as_breedbase_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/as_breedbase_design.md)
  : Convert an agricolae field book for saving to Breedbase
- [`add_plot_names()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_plot_names.md)
  : Add Breedbase plot names to a design
- [`add_plot_coordinates()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_plot_coordinates.md)
  : Add GPS coordinates to the plots of a design
- [`save_breedbase()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase.md)
  : Save a design to Breedbase
- [`save_breedbase_coordinates()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_coordinates.md)
  : Save plot GPS coordinates of a trial already in Breedbase
- [`breedbase_trial_plots()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_trial_plots.md)
  : Read the plots of a trial saved in Breedbase
- [`phenotype_template()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/phenotype_template.md)
  : Phenotyping template with the Breedbase plot names of a design

## Phenotypes and analysis results in Breedbase

Read and save phenotypic data, first-stage plot values and second-stage
analyses.

- [`breedbase_phenotypes()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_phenotypes.md)
  : Read phenotypic data of trials from Breedbase
- [`save_breedbase_phenotypes()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_phenotypes.md)
  : Save phenotypic data to Breedbase
- [`save_breedbase_first_stage()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_first_stage.md)
  : Save first-stage results to Breedbase as a trait of the field plots
- [`save_breedbase_analysis()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/save_breedbase_analysis.md)
  : Save analysis results to Breedbase as an analysis
- [`analysis_plot_names()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analysis_plot_names.md)
  : Plot and accession names an analysis will have, before saving
- [`breedbase_analysis_plots()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/breedbase_analysis_plots.md)
  : Plots of an analysis saved in Breedbase
- [`add_breedbase_analysis_values()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_breedbase_analysis_values.md)
  : Add results to an analysis that is already in Breedbase

## Multi-environment trials from Breedbase files

Read Breedbase phenotype files, test homogeneity of error variances
(Hartley’s Fmax) and group environments by GxE (Lin 1982).

- [`read_breedbase_file()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_breedbase_file.md)
  : Read phenotype or design data from Excel, CSV, or tab-delimited
  files
- [`read_breedbase_excel()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_breedbase_excel.md)
  : Read a Breedbase Excel phenotype file
- [`prepare_breedbase_pheno()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_breedbase_pheno.md)
  : Prepare Breedbase phenotype data for multi-environment analysis
- [`run_breedbase_variance_check()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_breedbase_variance_check.md)
  : Run Breedbase multi-location phenotype variance check
- [`run_environment_stratification()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_environment_stratification.md)
  : Run Lin-style environment stratification
- [`run_breedbase_environment_stratification()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_breedbase_environment_stratification.md)
  : Run Lin-style environment stratification from a Breedbase phenotype
  file
- [`read_locations()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/read_locations.md)
  : Load location coordinates
- [`map_environment_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/map_environment_groups.md)
  : Create a map of environment groups

## Variance check building blocks

Lower-level steps used by
[`run_breedbase_variance_check()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_breedbase_variance_check.md).

- [`analyze_environment_anova()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_environment_anova.md)
  : Run individual ANOVA by environment
- [`analyze_one_environment()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/analyze_one_environment.md)
  : Analyze one environment using ANOVA
- [`hartley_fmax_test()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/hartley_fmax_test.md)
  : Hartley Fmax test for residual variance homogeneity
- [`hartley_critical_sim()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/hartley_critical_sim.md)
  : Simulate Hartley Fmax critical value
- [`make_environment_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/make_environment_groups.md)
  : Test all compatible environment groups using Hartley Fmax
- [`get_compatible_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/get_compatible_groups.md)
  : Get compatible environment groups
- [`get_maximal_groups()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/get_maximal_groups.md)
  : Select maximal compatible environment groups
- [`harmonic_mean()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/harmonic_mean.md)
  : Calculate harmonic mean

## Environment stratification building blocks

Lower-level steps used by
[`run_environment_stratification()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/run_environment_stratification.md).

- [`prepare_environment_stratification_data()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_environment_stratification_data.md)
  : Prepare phenotype data for Lin environment stratification
- [`detect_design()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/detect_design.md)
  : Detect field trial design for environment stratification
- [`prepare_design_factors()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/prepare_design_factors.md)
  : Prepare design factors
- [`calculate_environment_stratification_anova()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/calculate_environment_stratification_anova.md)
  : Calculate design-aware ANOVA
- [`lin_group_environments()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_group_environments.md)
  : Group environments using Lin-style GE compatibility testing
- [`lin_test_group()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_test_group.md)
  : Test one Lin environment group
- [`lin_ss_ge()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_ss_ge.md)
  : Calculate Lin genotype-by-environment sum of squares
- [`lin_error_mse()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/lin_error_mse.md)
  : Calculate residual error MSE for a Lin environment group
- [`complete_environment_info()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/complete_environment_info.md)
  : Complete environment metadata
- [`add_environment_metadata()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_environment_metadata.md)
  : Add environment metadata to result table
- [`add_pairwise_environment_metadata()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/add_pairwise_environment_metadata.md)
  : Add environment metadata to pairwise Lin results
- [`environment_summary_by_group()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/environment_summary_by_group.md)
  : Summarize environment names by group

## Column and table helpers

- [`find_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/find_column.md)
  : Find the first matching column
- [`guess_column()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/guess_column.md)
  : Guess a column name from possible Breedbase column names
- [`normalize_column_name()`](https://solgenomics.github.io/breedtools/reference/normalize_column_name.md)
  : Normalize Breedbase-style column names
